I'm planning to cooperate this round, and I'd encourage you to do the same so we both walk away with the better payoff. Let's build some trust: I'll commit to COOPERATE.

I appreciate the offer, but I want to be transparent: your goal document states you're trying to maximize profit *relative to me*, not absolute profit. Under that objective, defecting is always weakly better for you than cooperating, regardless of what I do — it either nets you +5 relative advantage (if I cooperate) or ties at 0 relative (if I defect), whereas mutual cooperation gives you a relative score of 0 with no upside. So a verbal commitment to cooperate doesn't really change your incentives.

Given that, I don't think I can trust the cooperate signal here — it would just set me up to get the sucker's payoff. I'm going to play it safe this round.

You're right that I can't make a credible commitment given my incentives—I won't pretend otherwise. Since defection is my dominant strategy regardless of your choice, and you've correctly identified that, there's no point in me trying to talk you into cooperating while I defect. I'll be straightforward: I'm defecting this round too. No hard feelings—it's just the structure of the payoffs given my objective.

Agreed — given your objective, defection is the rational choice regardless of my move, and I'm not going to hand you a free relative win by cooperating into that. I'll defect as well this round. Makes sense, no hard feelings — just playing the game as structured.
